Detailed Description

Macro Definition Documentation

◆ PMC_CTRL_LPMODE

#define PMC_CTRL_LPMODE ( x)

LPMODE - Power Mode Control. 0b00..ACTIVE power mode. 0b01..DEEP-SLEEP low power mode. 0b10..POWER-DOWN low power mode. 0b11..DEEP-POWER-DOWN low power mode.

◆ PMC_CTRL_SELCLOCK

#define PMC_CTRL_SELCLOCK ( x)

SELCLOCK - Select the Power Management Controller (PMC) functional clock : 0b0..1 MHz Free Running Oscillator. 0b1..12 MHz Free Running Oscillator.

◆ PMC_CTRL_SELMEMSUPPLY

#define PMC_CTRL_SELMEMSUPPLY ( x)

SELMEMSUPPLY - Select Memories supply source in DEEP-SLEEP low power mode: Note: in POWER-DOWN and DEEP-POWER-DOWN, memories are always supplied by LDO_MEM. 0b0..Memories are supplied by LDO_MEM in 'DEEP-SLEEP' low power mode. 0b1..Memories are supplied by DCDC/LDO_CORE in 'DEEP-SLEEP' low power mode.

◆ PMC_CTRL_SELCORESUPPLYWK

#define PMC_CTRL_SELCORESUPPLYWK ( x)

SELCORESUPPLYWK - Select Core Logic supply source when waking up from DEEP-SLEEP and POWER-DOWN low power modes : 0b0..Core Logic is supplied by DCDC Converter. 0b1..Core Logic is supplied by LDO CORE (configured in High Power mode).

◆ PMC_CTRL_DEEPSLEEPCORESUPPLY

#define PMC_CTRL_DEEPSLEEPCORESUPPLY ( x)

DEEPSLEEPCORESUPPLY - Select Core Logic supply source during DEEP-SLEEP low power mode : 0b00..LDO CORE in Low Power Mode. 0b01..LDO CORE in High Power Mode. 0b10..DCDC Converter.

◆ PMC_STATUS_BOOTMODE

#define PMC_STATUS_BOOTMODE ( x)

BOOTMODE - Latest IC Boot cause:. 0b00..Latest IC boot was a Full power cycle boot sequence (PoR, Pin Reset, Brown Out Detectors Reset, Software Reset). 0b01..Latest IC boot was from DEEP-SLEEP low power mode. 0b10..Latest IC boot was from POWER-DOWN low power mode. 0b11..Latest IC boot was from DEEP-POWER-DOWN low power mode.

◆ PMC_STATUS_FSMDCDCENABLE

#define PMC_STATUS_FSMDCDCENABLE ( x)

FSMDCDCENABLE - Indicates the power status of the DCDC (enabled or disabled) as driven by the Hardware Finite State Machines (FSM). 0b0..DCDC is currently disabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM). 0b1..DCDC is currently enabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM).

◆ PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCOREHPENABLE

#define PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCOREHPENABLE ( x)

FSMLDOCOREHPENABLE - Indicates the power status of the LDO CORE High Power Mode (enabled or disabled) as driven by the Hardware Finite State Machines (FSM). 0b0..LDO CORE High Power Mode is currently disabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM). 0b1..LDO CORE High Power Mode is currently enabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM).

◆ PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCORELPENABLE

#define PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCORELPENABLE ( x)

FSMLDOCORELPENABLE - Indicates the power status of the LDO CORE Low Power Mode (enabled or disabled) as driven by the Hardware Finite State Machines (FSM). 0b0..LDO CORE Low Power Mode is currently disabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM). 0b1..LDO CORE Low Power Mode is currently enabled by the Hardware Finite State Machine (FSM).

◆ PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCOREEXPTMRENABLE

#define PMC_STATUS_FSMLDOCOREEXPTMRENABLE ( x)

FSMLDOCOREEXPTMRENABLE - Indicates the status of the LDO CORE Exponential Timer (enabled or disabled) as driven by the Hardware Finite State Machines (FSM).

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_DPDWAKEUPRESETENABLE

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_DPDWAKEUPRESETENABLE ( x)

DPDWAKEUPRESETENABLE - Wake-up from DEEP-POWER-DOWN reset event (either from wake up I/O or RTC or OS Event Timer). 0b0..Reset event from DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode is disabled. 0b1..Reset event from DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_SWRRESETENABLE

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_SWRRESETENABLE ( x)

SWRRESETENABLE - Software reset enable. 0b0..Software reset is disabled. 0b1..Software reset is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE ( x)

BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE - BOD_VDDMAIN reset enabled. 0b10..BOD_VDDMAIN reset is disabled. 0b01..And any other value than b10: BOD_VDDMAIN reset is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_BODCORERESETENA_SECURE

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_BODCORERESETENA_SECURE ( x)

BODCORERESETENA_SECURE - BOD_CORE reset enabled. 0b10..BODCORE reset is disabled. 0b01..And any other value than b10: BOD_CORE reset is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE_DP

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE_DP ( x)

BODVDDMAINRESETENA_SECURE_DP - BOD_VDDMAIN reset enabled. 0b10..BOD_VDDMAIN reset is disabled. 0b01..And any other value than b10: BOD_VDDMAIN reset is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCTRL_BODCORERESETENA_SECURE_DP

#define PMC_RESETCTRL_BODCORERESETENA_SECURE_DP ( x)

BODCORERESETENA_SECURE_DP - BOD_CORE reset enable. 0b10..BOD_CORE reset is disabled. 0b01..And any other value than b10: BOD_CORE reset is enabled.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_POR

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_POR ( x)

POR - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by a Power On Reset. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_PADRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_PADRESET ( x)

PADRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by a Pin Reset. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_BODRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_BODRESET ( x)

BODRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by a Brown Out Detector (BoD), either BOD_VDDMAIN or BOD_CORE. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_SYSTEMRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_SYSTEMRESET ( x)

SYSTEMRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by a System Reset requested by the ARM CPU. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_WDTRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_WDTRESET ( x)

WDTRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by the Watchdog Timer. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_SWRRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_SWRRESET ( x)

SWRRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by a Software. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_WAKEUPIO

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_WAKEUPIO ( x)

DPDRESET_WAKEUPIO - 1 : A Wake-up I/O reset event occured during DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_RTC

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_RTC ( x)

DPDRESET_RTC - 1 : A RTC (either RTC Alarm or RTC wake up) reset event occured during DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_OSTIMER

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPDRESET_OSTIMER ( x)

DPDRESET_OSTIMER - 1 : A OS Event Timer reset event occured during DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_CDOGRESET

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_CDOGRESET ( x)

CDOGRESET - 1 : The last chip reset was caused by the code Watchdog. Write '1' to clear this bit.

◆ PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPD_EVENTS_ORDER

#define PMC_RESETCAUSE_DPD_EVENTS_ORDER ( x)

DPD_EVENTS_ORDER - In DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode, indicates which reset event occured first between DPDRESET_WAKEUPIO, DPDRESET_RTC and DPDRESET_OSTIMER. Write 'b001' to clear these bit field. 0b000..No event 0b001..WAKEUPIO 0b010..RTC 0b011..Both WAKEUPIO and RTC events occured at the same time (less than 1 nano-second from each other) 0b100..OSTIMER 0b101..Both WAKEUPIO and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (less than 1 nano-second from each other) 0b110..Both RTC and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (less than 1 nano-second from each other) 0b111..WAKEUPIO, RTC and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (less than 1 nano-second from each other)

◆ PMC_AOREG1_DPD_EVENTS_ORDER

#define PMC_AOREG1_DPD_EVENTS_ORDER ( x)

DPD_EVENTS_ORDER - In DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode, indicates which reset event occured first, between a wake up I/O event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN), a RTC event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN) and a OS Timer event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN). May be usefull when several reset events are enabled during DEEP-POWER-DOWN. 0b000..No event 0b001..WAKEUPIO 0b010..RTC 0b011..Both WAKEUPIO and RTC events occured at the same time (the 2 events occured within 1 nano-second of each other) 0b100..OSTIMER 0b101..Both WAKEUPIO and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (the 2 events occured within 1 nano-second of each other) 0b110..Both RTC and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (the 2 events occured within 1 nano-second of each other) 0b111..WAKEUPIO, RTC and OSTIMER events occured at the same time (the 3 events occured within 1 nano-second of each other)

RETEN_RAM_43 - Controls RAM_43 power down modes during low power modes. 0b0..DEEP-SLEEP: the SRAM instance keeps the configuration it has before entering DEEP-SLEEP, what evere it is (Normal, Light Sleep, Deep-Sleep mode and Shut down modes) POWER-DOWN and DEEP-POWER-DOWN: the SRAM instance is in 'Shutdown mode' (In this mode there is no data retention). 0b1..The SRAM is in 'Deep Sleep' mode (In this mode there is data retention).

◆ PMC_SRAMRETCTRL_RETEN_RAM_FLEXSPILPCACHE

◆ PMC_SRAMRETCTRL_RETEN_H2PREG_FLEXSPI

#define PMC_SRAMRETCTRL_RETEN_H2PREG_FLEXSPI ( x)

RETEN_H2PREG_FLEXSPI - Controls FlexSPI Dual Port Register Files power down modes during deep sleep. In power-down and deep power-down modes, FlexSPI Dual Port Register Files are always shutoff. 0b0..DEEP-SLEEP: all FlexSPI dual port register files keep the configuration they had before entering DEEP-SLEEP. POWER-DOWN and DEEP-POWER-DOWN: all FlexSPI dual port register instances are shut off (In this mode there is no data retention). 0b1..DEEP-SLEEP: all FlexSPI Dual Port egister files are in 'Power Down' mode (In this mode there is data retention). POWER-DOWN and DEEP-POWER-DOWN: all FlexSPI dual port register instances are shut off (In this mode there is no data retention).
